title: Advanced Life Support (ALS) First Responder Service Operating Certificate
description: If you give advanced life support care, you need an operating certificate. This certificate is from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH). It does not let you move patients.

title: Ambulance Service Operating Certificate
description: If you run an ambulance business, you must register with the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Apparel Industry Certificate of Registration
description: Businesses that make clothes must register every year with the New York State Department of Labor (NYSDOL). This includes:

title: Asbestos Handler Certification
description: An asbestos handler is someone who is paid to remove, repair or enclose materials that have asbestos. To do this job, you need special training from a center approved by the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH). You also need certification from the New York State Department of Labor (NYSDOL) and the New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP).

title: Asbestos Handler Supervisor Certification
description: An asbestos handler supervisor leads the removal, repair or enclosure of materials with asbestos. To become one, you need special training from a New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) approved center. You also need certification from the New York State Department of Labor (NYSDOL) and the New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP).

title: Asbestos Investigator Certification
description: An asbestos investigator checks buildings for asbestos-containing materials (ACM) and conducts hazard assessments for ACM. To do this job, you need a special certificate and experience or technical training.

title: Assumed Name, Certificate of
description: If your business uses a name that is not its legal name, you need a Certificate of Assumed Name. This certificate is also called a "doing business as" (DBA) certificate. You must file this certificate with the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS).

title: ATV Dealer, Official Business Certificate
description: If you buy, sell or trade all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), you need to register with the New York State (NYS) Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV).

title: Backflow Prevention Device Tester Certification
description: People who test backflow prevention devices need training and certification from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Bank Holding Company Registration Certificate
description: If you have a bank holding company in New York State, you must register with the New York State (NYS) Department of Financial Services (DFS).

title: Banking/Trust Company Charter, Authorization Certificate
description: To start a bank or trust in New York State, you need a charter from the New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS). The charter allows your company to do business.

title: Bedding (Used) Retailer / Wholesaler
description: If your business sell used mattresses, you need a license from the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS).

title: Bedding Manufacturer (New Bedding)
description: If your business manufactures bedding, you need a license from the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS).

title: Bedding Manufacturer, Repairer-Renovator, or Rebuilder (Used Bedding)
description: If your business fixes or renovates used bedding, you must register with the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS).

title: Boat Dealer, Official Business Certificate
description: If you buy or sell motor boats, you must register with the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV).

title: Bottled Water Facility, Certificate of Approval to Operate a
description: If your business bottles water, you need a special certificate from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Bulk Water Facility, Certificate of Approval to Operate a
description: If your business sells water in bulk for human consumption, you need a certificate from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Business Certificate for Sole Proprietorships and General Partnerships
description: If your business uses a name other than its legal name, you need a Certificate of Assumed Name from your county clerk. This certificate is also called a business certificate.

title: Certificate of Approval
description: City Fire Department

title: Certificate of Fitness Emergency One-Way Voice Announcement Personnel (F-53)
description: The City Fire Department has rules for all one-way emergency voice services. Only the FDNY or building workers with an F-53 Certificate of Fitness can use these services.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Citywide Fire Guard For Impairment (F-01)
description: If a required fire protection system is not working in a building, a fire watch is needed. A person with a Certificate of Fitness must do the fire watch.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Citywide Sprinkler Systems (S-12)
description: If you inspect, test and maintain sprinkler systems in New York City, you need a Certificate of Fitness.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Citywide Standpipe Systems (S-13)
description: The City Fire Department needs anyone who inspects, tests and maintains standpipe systems in New York City to have an S-13 or S-14 Certificate of Fitness.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Cleaning and Testing of Smoke Detectors (F-78 / S-78)
description: If you test and clean smoke detectors in New York City, you need a Certificate of Fitness for Cleaning and Testing of Smoke Detectors (F-78/S-78).

title: Certificate of Fitness for Commercial Cooking Exhaust System Cleaning Technician (W-64)
description: The New York City Fire Department (FDNY) says that commercial cooking exhaust systems must be cleaned by someone with a Certificate of Fitness (W-64/P-64). This person must work for an FDNY-approved company.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Coordinator of Fire Safety and Alarm Systems in Homeless Shelters (F-80)
description: The City Fire Department says all homeless shelters need a person with a Certificate of Fitness for Coordinator of Fire Safety and Alarm Systems in Homeless Shelters (F-80). This certificate is also needed in any building or occupancy that must have a one-way voice communication system. This applies if the building is used by more than 15 people for more than 30 days, including emergency shelters.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Fire Alarm Systems Inspection, Testing and Service Principal (S-97)
description: A principal of a company that installs, inspects, tests and services fire alarm systems in New York City needs a Certificate of Fitness for Fire Alarm Systems Inspection, Testing and Service Principal (S-97). You must know the manufacturer's recommendations for different fire alarm systems.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Fire Alarm Systems Inspection, Testing and Service Technician (S-98)
description: A technician who installs, inspects, tests and services fire alarm systems in New York City needs a Certificate of Fitness for Fire Alarm Systems Inspection, Testing and Service Technician (S-98).

title: Certificate of Fitness for Fire and Emergency Drill Conductor (F-07)
description: The City Fire Department offers a Certificate of Fitness for Fire and Emergency Drill Conductor.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Fire and Emergency Drill Conductor for NYC K-12 Schools (D-10)
description: Principals and assistant principals who lead fire drills in New York City K-12 schools must have a Certificate of Fitness for Fire and Emergency Drill Conductor (D-10).

title: Certificate of Fitness for Fire Guard for Shelters (F-02)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to be a Fire Guard in shelters if there is no sprinkler system or if the fire protection system is not working.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Fire Guard for Torch Operations (F-60)
description: A Certificate of Fitness holder must be present to watch for fires during hot work operations.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Fire Life and Safety Director (F89/T89)
description: A Fire and Life Safety (FLS) Director is needed in some buildings, including high-rise office buildings, hotels and buildings with special fire alarm systems. These buildings need a Comprehensive Fire Safety and Emergency Action Plan or are buildings that previously required Fire Safety Directors.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Flame Retardant Treatment (C-15)
description: The New York City Fire Department (FDNY) says that some places need flame-resistant decorations. These places include Groups A, E, I and M occupancies; Group R-1 college and university dorms; common areas in Groups B, R-1 and R-2 occupancies; and any building or place used for public gatherings.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Handling and Dispensing Flammable or Combustible Liquids in Portable Containers (S-94)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to handle and dispense flammable or combustible liquids in portable containers. These liquids include motor fuels like gasoline and diesel fuel.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Handling, Use and Storage of Flammable Compressed Gases (G-98)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to handle, use and store compressed flammable gases. This certificate is only valid for the person and location it is issued to.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Indoor Place of Assembly Safety Personnel (F-03)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to help support fire safety at a place of assembly (PA) or temporary place of assembly (TPA). This certificate is for a specific person and location.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Low Pressure Oil Burner Operator (P-99)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness (CoF) to supervise an oil burner that is not fully automatic or needs preheating. The certificate holder must be in the building when the burner is on.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Non-Production Chemical Laboratories (C-14)
description: You need a permit to store, handle or use dangerous materials in a lab if you have more than 1 gallon (3.8L) of flammable liquid, more than 1 gallon (3.8L) of combustible liquid and more than 75 SCF (2.12 m3) of flammable gas.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Operation of Petroleum Pipeline (P-23)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to operate petroleum pipelines. This certificate is only for the person it is given to. You can use it anywhere in New York City.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Operator of Central Station Signaling Systems (F-40)
description: If you work in a central station that reports fires in New York City, you need a Certificate of Fitness for Operator of Central Station Signaling Systems (F-40).

title: Certificate of Fitness for Powder Actuated Tools (E-21)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to use powder actuated tools. These tools can be dangerous, so you must create a safe zone behind the work area.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Residential Sprinkler Systems (S-11)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness from the City Fire Department. This is for people who inspect, test and maintain sprinkler systems in residential buildings or structures classified as R-2 occupancies. It is for buildings up to six stories high. These buildings can have up to 30 sprinkler heads or a compactor sprinkler system.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Safe Use, Handling, Storage and Compression of Flammable Gases with Pressure Above 6 PSI (G-29)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to use, handle, store and compress flammable gases with pressure above 6 psi. This certificate is only for the person it is given to. It can be used anywhere in New York City.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Special Effects (E-series)
description: The City Fire Department offers a Certificate of Fitness for Special Effects (E-series). This includes E-01, E-02, E-03, E-04, E-05 and E-06.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Standpipe for Multi-Zone Systems (S-14)
description: Buildings with multi-zone standpipe systems must be under the supervision of a person with an S-14 Certificate of Fitness. This certificate is only valid at one location and for the person who gets it.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Storage and Handling of Corrosives and Oxidizers (C-42)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to store and handle corrosives and oxidizers. This certificate is for a specific location and person.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Storage and Handling of LPG or CNG (G-44)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to store or handle liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) or compressed natural gas (CNG). These gases are extremely flammable, so safety is critical.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Storage, Handling and Use of Hazardous Materials (C-91)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to store, handle and use hazardous materials.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Supervising Dry Cleaning Facilities (C-93)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to supervise dry cleaning facilities that use Class II or III solvents. The certificate is for a specific location and person.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Supervising, Storage, Handling and Use of Flammable or Combustible Liquids (C-92)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to store, handle and use flammable or combustible liquids. This is required if you have a New York City Fire Department (FDNY) permit.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Supervision of Aerosol (W-49)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness if you have 100 pounds or more of aerosols. Aerosols are things like:

title: Certificate of Fitness for Supervision of Fire Alarm Systems and Other Related Systems (S-95)
description: Every building with a fire alarm system needs someone physically present with an S-95 Certificate of Fitness for supervision of fire alarm systems and other related systems.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Supervision of Flammable and Combustible Finishing Operations (C-30)
description: The City Fire Department offers a Certificate of Fitness to supervise flammable and combustible finishing operations:

title: Certificate of Fitness for Supervision of Piped Non-Flammable Medical Gases (G-71)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to supervise piped non-flammable medical gases. You must handle and store these gases safely. These gases include:

title: Certificate of Fitness for Supervision of Portable Fueled Space Heaters at Construction Sites (S-92)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to supervise portable fueled space heaters at construction sites. These heaters give temporary heat to buildings during construction.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Supervision of Sanitary Landfill Methane Recovery Facilities (L-19)
description: The City Fire Department offers a Certificate of Fitness to supervise sanitary landfill methane recovery facilities:

title: Certificate of Fitness for Supervision of Storage, Handling and Use of Commercial Cryogenic Systems (G-79)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to supervise the storage, handling and use of commercial cryogenic systems and liquids. You must be on-site at all times during operation if you have this certificate.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Temporary Indoor / Outdoor Place of Assembly Safety Personnel (F-04)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to help keep fire safety at temporary events. This certificate is valid only for the person it is issued to and can be used anywhere in New York City.

title: Certificate of Fitness for the Storage, Handling, Use and Refilling of Non-Flammable Gas Cylinders (G-46)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to store, handle, use or refill non-flammable gas cylinders. These cylinders are often used in health care places. Non-flammable gases include:

title: Certificate of Fitness for the Supervision and Maintenance of a CNG Facility (C-99)
description: The City Fire Department offers a Certificate of Fitness for dispensing, supervising and maintaining a compressed natural gas (CNG) facility:

title: Certificate of Fitness for the Supervision of Bulk Oil Storage Facility (P-13)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to supervise a bulk oil storage facility. A certificate holder must be there when the plant is running.

title: Certificate of Fitness for the Supervision of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Plants (C-10)
description: The City Fire Department offers a Certificate of Fitness for the supervision of liquified natural gas (LNG) plants:

title: Certificate of Fitness for the Use of LPG / CNG at Outdoors Events and for Mobile Cooking (G-23)
description: City Fire Department

title: Certificate of Fitness for the Use of LPG / CNG in Emergency Indoor Repairs (G-24)
description: The City Fire Department offers a Certificate of Fitness to handle liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) or compressed natural gas (CNG):

title: Certificate of Fitness for Torch Use in Manufacture of Jewelry and Dental Lab Operation (G-61)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to use an oxygen-fuel torch or any flammable gas torch in making jewelry and for dental lab work. You must control the pressure and flow of oxygen and natural gas to each torch.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Torch Use of Flammable Gases (G-60)
description: The City Fire Department needs you to have a Certificate of Fitness to use a torch with oxygen and a flammable gas. This includes using a torch for torch-applied roofing systems.

title: Certificate of Fitness for Use and Handling of LPG / CNG for Tar Kettles, Asphalt Melters and Marking Street Lines (G-40)
description: The City Fire Department offers a Certificate of Fitness to use and handle liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) or compressed natural gas (CNG):

title: Certificate of Fitness for Use of LPG or CNG in Engine Fuel Systems (G-22)
description: City Fire Department

title: Certificate of Fitness to Operate and Maintain Air Compressors (A-35)
description: The City Fire Department offers a Certificate of Fitness to operate and maintain air compressors:

title: Certificate of Fitness to Supervise Crane Aerial Fueling Operations at Construction Sites (P-54)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to supervise aerial crane fueling at construction sites and other locations. This includes using diesel fuel or other flammable liquids.

title: Certificate of Fitness to Supervise Temporary Storage & Dispensing Flammable/Combustible Liquids at Movie/TV Prod.Sites (S-91)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness to supervise the temporary storage and dispensing of flammable or combustible liquids at movie and TV production sites.

title: Certificate of Fitness to Supervise the Handling and Use of Chemicals in NYC K-12 School Laboratories (D-14)
description: All teachers who use labs in NYC K-12 schools need a Certificate of Fitness. This certificate is for handling and using chemicals. The certificate is valid only at a specific location and for the person it is issued to.

title: Certificate of Fitness to Supervise the Storage and Handling of Chemicals in NYC K-12 School Laboratories (D-15)
description: All lab workers who store and handle chemicals in NYC K-12 schools need a Certificate of Fitness (D-15). This certificate is valid only at a specific location and for the person it is issued to.

title: Certificate of Incorporation for Corporations, Professional Service Corporations, and Not-for-Profit Corporations
description: All corporations in New York State must file a Certificate of Incorporation with the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS).

title: Certificate of Occupancy
description: A Certificate of Occupancy (CO) tells you how you can legally use a building.

title: Certificate of Qualification for Refrigerating System Operating Engineer (Q-01)
description: If a refrigerating system needs a permit from the New York City Fire Department (FDNY), you need a Certificate of Qualification (Q01) to watch the system while it is running. This certificate is specific to the location.

title: Certificate of Registration for Expeditor (Filing Processor) Employee (R-02)
description: City Fire Department

title: Certificate of Registration for Expeditor (Filing Processor) Principal (R-01)
description: The New York City Fire Department (FDNY) requires a Certificate of Registration for Expeditor (Filing Processor) Principal (R-01) .

title: Certified First Responder (CFR) Certificate
description: In New York State, you need a certificate to be a first responder. The Certified First Responder (CFR) Certificate comes from the New York State (NYS) Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Certified Home Health Agency (CHHA), Operating Certificate
description: Home health agencies must be certified to operate in New York State. This certificate is from the NYS Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Clinical Laboratory Director or Assistant Director Certificate of Qualification
description: To be a director or assistant director of a clinical lab, you need a certificate from the Wadsworth Center of the New York State Department of Health. Laboratories must have a certified director to get a permit.

title: COF to Supervise the Temporary Storage and Dispensing of Flammable or Combustible Liquids at Construction Sites (S-93)
description: You need a Certificate of Fitness (COF) to watch over the storage and use of flammable or combustible liquids at construction sites. This certificate is only valid for the person it is issued to and can be used anywhere in New York City.

title: Continuing Care Retirement Community & Fee-for-Service Continuing Care Retirement Community Operating Certificate
description: Nursing and retirement homes need an operating certificate from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH). It is for facilities that offer continuing care for a fee. These places operate to improve quality of life, not to provide medical care.

title: Corporation, Certificate of Incorporation in New York State
description: If you start a new corporation in New York State, you must file a Certificate of Incorporation with the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS).

title: Diagnostic and Treatment Center (Clinic), Operating Certificate
description: In New York State, diagnostic and treatment centers (clinics) need a certificate from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Driving School Instructor Certificate
description: If you want to teach at a driving school, you need a Driving School Instructor Certificate from the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV).

title: Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Certification
description: To become a Certified First Responder (CFR) or an Emergency Medical Technician (EMT), you need to train with an approved course provider. The New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) approves these providers. After you finish the training, you will get a certificate.

title: Enhanced Assisted Living Residence (EALR) Certification
description: Assisted living homes can get a special certificate called the Enhanced Assisted Living Residence (EALR) Certificate from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) to provide additional care.

title: Environmental Laboratory Approval Program (ELAP) Certification
description: The New York State Department of Health (DOH) requires commercial, noncommercial and government labs to get an Environmental Laboratory Approval Program (ELAP) Certification. This is needed to test environmental samples from New York State.

title: Euthanize Animals, Certificate to
description: Organizations must have a certificate to euthanize animals. This certificate is issued by the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Food Processing Plant Certification
description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) must check and approve all food made at a food processing plant.

title: Food Protection Certificate
description: The NYC Health Academy offers a food protection course for restaurant managers, operators and other staff. Anyone can take this class.

title: Foster Care Operating Certificate
description: Foster care residential programs need a Foster Care Operating Certificate from the New York State Office of Child and Family Services (OCFS).

title: Funeral Firm Certificate of Registration
description: Funeral firms must register with the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH). They must meet facility requirement. They must follow laws and rules on customer rights and the treatment of human remains.

title: Hazardous Substance Bulk Storage Registration Certificate
description: If you want to store hazardous substances in bulk, you need a Registration Certificate. The New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) gives this certificate.

title: Hospice Facility, Operating Certificate
description: Hospices and palliative care facilities need a certificate to operate in New York State. This certificate comes from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Hospital, Operating Certificate
description: Hospitals in New York State need two certificates: an Operating Certificate and a Certificate of Need. Both come from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Hypodermic Syringes and Needles, Certificate of Need to Possess
description: Businesses and individuals who need hypodermic syringes for professional reasons must obtain a certificate issued by the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Interior Design Certification
description: In New York State, you need a license to be a "Certified Interior Designer." The New York State Education Department (NYSED) issues this certificate.

title: Juvenile Detention Facility, Certificate to Operate
description: You need this certificate to run a juvenile detention facility. The New York State Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS) gives out this certificate.

title: Limited Liability Company (Foreign), Certificate of Authority
description: If your limited liability company (LLC) is from another state, you can register for a Certificate of Authority in New York State. You need to register with the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS).

title: Long-Term Home Health Care Program (LTHHCP), Operating Certificate
description: Home health care programs need a certificate from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Mobile Laser Operator, Certificate of Competence
description: You need a certificate to use a mobile laser in New York State. Mobile laser operators must meet requirements for education and experience.

title: Motor Vehicle Repair Shop, Official Business Certificate
description: If you repair motor vehicles, you need a certificate from the New York State DMV.

title: Not-for-Profit, Certificate of Incorporation
description: Not-for-profit corporations (non-profits) must file a Certificate of Incorporation with the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS).

title: Nursery Dealer Registration Certificate
description: If you have a business that buys or gets plant nursery stock to resell, you must register with the New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets.

title: Pesticide Applicator (Commercial) Certification
description: If you use pesticides for a business, you need a Pesticide Applicator (Commercial) Certification. The New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) gives this permit.

title: Pesticide Applicator (Private) Certification
description: If you use pesticides for agriculture, you need a Pesticide Applicator (Private) Certification. The New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) gives this permit.

title: Place of Assembly Certificate of Operation
description: A Place of Assembly Certificate of Operation (PA) shows that places where many people gather are safe. The Department of Buildings (DOB) issues this certificate.

title: Plant Grower Registration Certificate
description: If you grow plants to sell, you need to register with the New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets.

title: Private School Agent Certificate
description: If you want to recruit students for a private adult school or trade school, you need a certificate. This certificate lets you be a private school agent. The New York State Education Department (NYSED) gives out this certificate.

title: Processing Plant Superintendent Certification
description: The State Agriculture and Markets Department says every dairy business needs a certified Processing Plant Superintendent. This person makes sure the plant is clean and safe.

title: Radiation Installation, Certificate of Registration for
description: If you install radiation equipment in New York State, you need a certificate from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Radiation Producing Equipment - Certificate of Registration
description: If you own or use any radiation equipment for patient care, you need a Radiation Producing Equipment - Certificate of Registration from the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH). You need this certificate to set up, keep or use the equipment. Registrations are sorted by facility and permit type. You must renew your registration every two years.

title: Regents Charter / Certificate of Incorporation
description: Educational institutions in New York need a charter or certificate of incorporation. The New York State Board of Regents gives these.

title: Residential Facility for Victims of Domestic Violence, Operating Certificate
description: The New York State Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS) gives the Operating Certificate. This certificate is for places that help victims of domestic violence, which can be physical, emotional or financial abuse. It can happen in romantic or parent-child relationships. OCFS protects victims and checks these places.

title: Restricted Asbestos Handler Certification
description: The Restricted Asbestos Handler Certification is for workers trained at any of the New York State Department of Health approved centers. These workers are certified by the New York State Department of Labor (NYSDOL) and the New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP). They perform construction work in preparation for or to assist in the actual abatement work.

title: Runaway and Homeless Youth Shelter, Operating Certificate
description: Homeless youth shelters need permits from the New York State Office of Children and Family Services (OCFS). OCFS works with the New York City Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) to oversee shelters in New York City.

title: Safe Deposit Company Branch Office, Authorization Certificate
description: This certificate lets a safe deposit company open a new branch. The State Banking Department gives this certificate.

title: Safe Deposit Company Charter, Authorization Certificate
description: This certificate lets a business run a safe deposit company.

title: Savings Bank Life Insurance Certificate Holder
description: People or businesses that handle life insurance need a certificate. This certificate is from the New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS). With it, savings banks can have departments to sell life insurance.

title: Scrap Collector, Official Business Certificate
description: If you collect and dispose of scrap metal from cars, you need a certificate. The New York State DMV gives this certificate. Repair shops must say they dispose of scrap on their Repair Shop application.

title: Scrap Processor, Official Business Certificate
description: Scrap processors buy vehicles to turn them into scrap. They are certified by the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV). Processors do not sell vehicles or their parts.

title: Seafood Delivery Business
description: If you deliver seafood in New York City, you need a Seafood Delivery Business Registration. This is for businesses that use trucks or other vehicles to deliver seafood from wholesalers to stores or other wholesalers.

title: Temporary Place of Assembly Certificate of Operation
description: Most events with limited durations need a Temporary Place of Assembly (TPA) Certificate of Operation (TPACO).

title: Temporary Waterfront Place of Assembly Certificate of Operation
description: You need a Temporary Waterfront Event Certificate for events on City-owned waterfront property. You need this certificate if:

title: Therapeutic Radiation (LINAC)- Certified Registration of Units
description: The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) gives Certified Registrations. This lets you use therapeutic radiation units (LINACs) to treat people.

title: Water Potability Certificate
description: The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene issues a Water Potability Certificate to wholesale food establishments. This certificate is needed if a government agency asks for it.

title: Waterfront Place of Assembly Certificate of Operation
description: You need a special permit called a Place of Assembly (PA) Certificate of Operation if:

title: Wholesale Seafood Business
description: You need a Wholesale Seafood Business Registration to sell seafood at a New York City public wholesale market and sell seafood for resale to the public. If you sell seafood that another business has processed and packaged, you are not a wholesaler.

title: Workplace Safety and Loss Prevention Consultant Certificate
description: You need a license to give advice on workplace safety and workers' compensation. This license is from the New York State Department of Labor.

title: Yacht Broker, Official Business Certificate
description: This certificate lets you help someone buy or sell a boat or yacht.

title: Accelerated Sales Tax Exemption Program (ASTEP)
description: The Accelerated Sales Tax Exemption Program (ASTEP) helps businesses buy equipment or make renovations without paying sales tax. The New York City Industrial Development Agency (NYCIDA) runs ASTEP.

title: Business Incentive Rate
description: The Business Incentive Rate (BIR) is an energy discount program run by the New York City Economic Development Corporation (EDC) and Con Edison. The EDC can provide BIR benefits.

title: Commercial and Industrial Energy Efficiency Program
description: The Con Edison Commercial and Industrial Energy Efficiency (CIEE) Program gives cash rebates and incentives for energy-saving projects. Projects include installing energy-efficient equipment and technology. Only Con Edison gas and electric customers can join.

title: Commercial Expansion Program
description: The Commercial Expansion Program (CEP) helps fill occupancy in offices and industrial spaces. CEP gives property tax benefits for new, renewal and expansion leases. These spaces must be built before January 1, 1999, and must be in a special zone. Applicants must also make some physical improvements to the spaces and common areas.

title: Commercial Revitalization Program
description: The Commercial Revitalization Program (CRP) helps improve some areas of the City. It focuses on older business areas and increasing office and store use. The program's tax benefits include property tax abatements and Commercial Rent Tax reductions. Eligible buildings must be nonresidential or mixed-use built before 1975 and located in specific abatement zones.

title: Disabled Access Credit and Additional Tax Deduction for Barrier Removal Costs for the Disabled or Elderly
description: Businesses can use two federal tax incentives to help cover the costs of making access improvements for customers with disabilities or the elderly. These incentives help businesses follow the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

title: EDC Incentives
description: The New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC) can help lower project costs via tax incentives and bond financing. These incentives come from two groups:

title: Emerging Business Enterprise (EBE) Certification Program
description: The Emerging Business Enterprise (EBE) Certification Program helps businesses owned, operated and controlled by people who face social and economic disadvantages. These businesses get special help with New York City contracts. The goal is to make city contracts fairer for these business owners.

title: Employment Incentive Credit
description: The Employment Incentive Credit (EIC) is a tax credit for businesses in New York State. If your business claims the Investment Tax Credit (ITC) and creates new jobs, you may get the EIC for the next two years.

title: Empowerment Zone Wage Tax Credit
description: The Empowerment Zone Wage Tax Credit helps businesses in special areas called Empowerment Zones. They were created to encourage business growth and economic development in low-income communities. New York City has two Empowerment Zones. One is in Upper Manhattan. The other is in the South Bronx.

title: Energy Cost Savings Program
description: The Energy Cost Savings Program (ECSP) helps businesses save money on energy. It can cut energy costs by up to 45 percent and natural gas costs by up to 35 percent. These savings last for eight years. After that, the savings go down by 20 percent each year for four more years.

title: Excelsior Jobs Program
description: The Excelsior Jobs Program helps businesses in certain industries in New York State. Businesses can get tax credits over 10 years for investing and creating new jobs.

title: Food Retail Expansion to Support Health (FRESH) Program
description: The Food Retail Expansion to Support Health (FRESH) program helps bring grocery stores to neighborhoods that need them. It offers zoning and financial incentives to make this happen.

title: Green Roof Property Tax Abatement Program
description: The Green Roof Property Tax Abatement gives a one-year tax break. This is for building a green roof on homes and businesses in New York City. This program helps the City's long-term sustainability plan, PlaNYC.

title: Incentives Estimator
description: The NYC Business Incentives Estimator helps businesses find and learn about city, state, and federal incentives that are directly applicable to their operations. By answering a series of questions regarding their businesses activities, location, and size, users receive a list of incentives programs they are estimated to be eligible for. Additionally, the Incentives Estimator also provides users with pro forma calculations for estimated savings with an estimated yearly benefit schedule based on their answers. Please note that the Incentives Estimator is now updated.

title: Incentives for Exporters
description: Businesses that export or import goods can get help from the state and federal government.

title: Industrial and Commercial Abatement Program (ICAP)
description: The Industrial and Commercial Abatement Program (ICAP) helps lower property taxes for up to 25 years for industrial and commercial buildings that are updated, expanded or improved. ICAP replaced the Industrial Commercial Exemption Program (ICIP) in 2008. ICIP benefits approved before 2008 are still valid.

title: Industrial Business Zone Relocation Credit
description: The Industrial Business Zone (IBZ) Relocation Tax Credit is a one-time tax credit. It gives $1,000 per moved worker to industrial and manufacturing firms. These firms must move to one of the City's 21 IBZs. Firms moving within an IBZ can also get this credit.

title: Industrial Effectiveness Program
description: The Industrial Effectiveness Program helps factories improve and grow. Empire State Development runs this program.

title: Investment Tax Credit
description: Businesses in New York State can get a tax credit when they invest in buildings, machines or equipment. This credit is called the Investment Tax Credit (ITC).

title: Locally Based Enterprise (LBE) Certification Program
description: The Locally-Based Enterprise (LBE) Certification Program helps businesses in poor areas of the city. It also helps businesses that hire economically disadvantaged people. These businesses get at least 10% of subcontracting opportunities on City construction jobs.

title: Lower Manhattan Energy Program
description: The Lower Manhattan Energy Program (LMEP) helps property owners and business renters save money on electricity. They can save up to 45% on electricity costs. These savings last for eight years. After that, the savings go down by 20% each year for four more years.

title: Lower Manhattan Relocation Employment Assistance for Eligible Businesses
description: The Lower Manhattan Relocation and Employment Assistance Program for Eligible Businesses (LMREAP-EB) gives tax credits to businesses that move to Lower Manhattan. Your business has to move at least one employee from outside the LMREAP-EB area to a qualified location to be eligible.

title: Lower Manhattan Relocation Employment Assistance Program for Special Eligible Businesses
description: The Lower Manhattan Relocation and Employment Assistance Program for Special Eligible Businesses (LMREAP-SEB) helps businesses that move to Lower Manhattan that do not qualify for the Lower Manhattan Relocation and Employment Assistance Program for Eligible Businesses (LMREAP-EB) because they already had employees in Manhattan before relocation. To apply, your business must move from outside the City to a qualified location.

title: Made in NY Marketing Credit
description: The "Made in NY" Marketing Credit program helps film and TV shows get free co-branded ads in New York City, the U.S.'s top media market. To qualify, at least 75 percent of your film or TV show must be made in New York City.

title: Manufacturing Assistance Program
description: The Manufacturing Assistance Program provides monetary grants for manufacturing businesses. Grants are for projects to improve productivity or competitiveness.

title: Minority and Women-owned Business Enterprise (M/WBE) Certification Program
description: The City of New York Minority and Women-owned Business Enterprise (M/WBE) Program helps you, as a minority and/or women entrepreneur, access government contracts and grow your businesses. When you get certified with the City, your business becomes more visible to buyers, including City agencies and private contractors looking to purchase goods and services.

title: National Grid Commercial and Industrial Efficiency Program
description: National Grid's Commercial and Industrial Efficiency Program helps businesses in New York City save on natural gas. This program used to be called the Economic Development Gas Rate (EDGAR).

title: New Markets Revolving Loan Fund
description: The New Markets Revolving Loan Fund (NMRLF) is a federal program to help small business owners in low-income areas get loans. The program gives money to loan providers, then the providers must match the funds dollar for dollar.

title: New Markets Tax Credit Program
description: The New Markets Tax Credit (NMTC) is a federal program that helps provide money for buying, building and fixing up buildings in low-income areas. This includes:

title: New York City Brownfield Incentive Grant (BIG) Program, Pre-Development Design Grant
description: The Pre-Development Design Grant helps with early planning for brownfield redevelopment. Brownfields are empty or underused sites where environmental contamination may complicate redevelopment or reuse. These grants help with redevelopment planning before environmental field investigation and clean up.

title: NYC Accelerator Services
description: NYC Accelerator offers free, personalized guidance to help your building use less energy, saving you money and helping the environment. The program also helps you follow New York City's rules for cutting greenhouse gases (Local Law 97 and the Climate Mobilization Act).

title: NYC BioTech Tax Credit
description: The Biotechnology Tax Credit helps investors and owners of qualified emerging technology companies (QETCs) focused on biotechnology to claim a tax credit for certain costs in New York City. These costs include:

title: NYC Clean Trucks Program
description: The NYC Clean Trucks Program is a rebate incentive funding program. It wascreated to reduce diesel exhaust emissions by replacing older diesel trucks.

title: NYCIDA Garment Center Program
description: The Garment Center Program is run by the New York City Industrial Development Agency (NYCIDA). It helps property owners who rent space to fashion manufacturers in the Garment District. The program gives real estate tax breaks.

title: NYS Thruway Commercial Charge Account Program
description: The Commercial Charge Account Program helps companies pay for tolls incurred in their business. The New York State Thruway Authority runs this program.

title: NYSERDA Agriculture Energy Audit Program
description: New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) helps agriculture businesses save energy. They offer energy checks for such businesses. Urban agriculture businesses such as greenhouses, vegetable growers and poultry producers can get help.

title: NYSERDA Commercial New Construction Program
description: The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) has a program called the Commercial New Construction Program (CNCP). This program helps businesses make new or renovated buildings more energy efficient. It offers technical support to building design teams and also gives financial incentives to building owners.

title: NYSERDA FlexTech Program
description: The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) FlexTech Program helps businesses in New York State make informed energy decisions. It gives custom advice to many types of organizations. These include commercial, industrial, government and not-for-profit groups.

title: NYSERDA Industrial and Process Efficiency Program
description: The Industrial and Process Efficiency Program helps manufacturers and data centers save energy.

title: NYSERDA On the Job Training
description: New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) helps clean energy businesses hire new workers. Businesses can get up to $100,000. NYSERDA will pay 50% of a new worker's wages for up to 16 weeks. For some workers, NYSERDA will pay for up to 24 weeks.

title: NYSERDA Real-Time Energy Management Program
description: The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) runs the Real-Time Energy Management (RTEM) program.

title: NYSERDA Small Commercial Energy Assessments
description: The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) gives free energy checks to small businesses and not-for-profit groups. These checks help these organizations make smart energy choices and save energy.

title: NYSERDA Transportation Programs
description: The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) helps transportation businesses save money on energy.

title: Property Tax Exemption for Non Profits
description: Organizations can get a full or partial cut in property taxes if they use the property for certain not-for-profit purposes.

title: Qualified Emerging Technology Company Certification and Capital Tax Credit
description: The Qualified Emerging Technology Company (QETC) Certification and Capital Tax Credit gives a tax credit to some businesses.

title: Qualified Emerging Technology Company Employment Credit
description: This credit rewards companies for creating jobs.

title: Relocation and Employment Assistance Program
description: The Relocation and Employment Assistance Program (REAP) helps businesses. It gives income tax credits for moving jobs to certain areas in New York City. If your business moves jobs from outside New York City or below 96th Street in Manhattan to areas above 96th Street or other boroughs, you can apply.

title: SBA 7(a) Loan Program
description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) offers 7(a) loans. These loans help small businesses. Commercial lenders give these loans.

title: SBA CDC / 504 Loan Program
description: The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) 504 loan program helps small businesses get money for new assets. These loans can be used for:

title: Small Business Commercial Direct Install
description: The Small Business Commercial Direct Install (CDI) program helps small businesses save energy. Con Edison runs this program.

title: Small Business Health Care Tax Credit
description: The Small Business Health Care Tax Credit helps small businesses that give health care coverage to their workers. This credit is for businesses with fewer than 25 full-time workers with average wages under $50,000 a year.

title: Solar Electric Generating Systems Tax Abatement Program
description: The Solar Electric Generating Systems Tax Abatement program helps people save money on taxes who build a solar electric generating system in their homes or businesses in New York City. This program is part of the City's plan to be more sustainable. It provides an incentive for building owners to use cleaner power and cut down on pollution.

title: State Minority- and Women- Owned Business Enterprise Program
description: The Minority- and Women-Owned Business Enterprise Program (MWBE) helps businesses owned by women and/or minorities in New York State. If you own, run and control a business as a woman or minority, you can join this program. The program gives these businesses priority for state government contracts.

title: Trade Adjustment Assistance Grant Program
description: The Trade Adjustment Assistance Grant helps businesses impacted by foreign competition. It is for manufacturers or service firms in New York, New Jersey or Puerto Rico.

title: Work Opportunity Tax Credit
description: The Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC) is a federal tax credit. It gives employers up to $9,600 for hiring people from certain groups.

title: Workers with Disabilities Employment Tax Credit
description: This tax credit helps employers hire people with disabilities.

title: Boiler Permit
description: All boilers in New York City must be inspected and certified by the Department of Buildings Boiler Unit.

title: Food Safety and Inspection Regulations
description: The federal government has rules for food safety covering the making and selling of food. Businesses must follow City, State and federal rules.

title: Hazardous Chemicals Inspection
description: The Fire Department of New York (FDNY) inspects for the proper storage of hazardous chemicals in New York City. These checks help keep people and buildings safe from fires caused by these chemicals.

title: Inspections and Testing
description: The Fire Department of New York (FDNY) inspects buildings and other places in New York City. They do this to make sure that code, laws, rules or regulations are being enforced to keep the public safe.

title: Permanent Amusement Ride Installation and Inspections
description: All amusement rides in New York City, like ferris wheels and carousels, must be inspected by the Department of Buildings (DOB). They also need a license from the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP).

title: Petroleum Measuring Devices Inspection
description: All devices that measure petroleum at a business must be tested and sealed. This includes:

title: Weighing and Measuring Devices / Inspections
description: The New York City (NYC) Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) inspects scales at businesses. They make sure the scales are correct. You can ask for a scale check online or by calling 311.

title: Weights and Measures / Gasoline and Home Heating Oil Delivery Truck Meters
description: New York State and New York City have laws about weights and measures. These laws say items must be sold by their true weight or measure. The NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) inspects scales and measuring devices. This includes gas pumps and home heating oil delivery truck meters. They make sure these devices work correctly.

title: Weights and Measures / Retail Gas Stations
description: New York State and New York City have laws about weights and measures. These laws make sure items are sold by their true weight or size. The NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) inspects gas stations every year. They also look into customer complaints to make sure the laws are followed.

title: Accident and Health Insurance License, Domestic
description: This license allows an insurer to conduct accident and health insurance business in New York State.

title: Accident and Health Insurance License, Foreign
description: Businesses from outside New York State need this license to provide accident and health coverage in New York.

title: Appearance Enhancement Business or Area Renter License
description: If you run a beauty business, you need a special license from the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS). This license is different from those for styling hair, doing manicures and other services.

title: Application for Permission to Disburse Net Proceeds of Bingo
description: Nonprofit groups in New York State need permission to use money from bingo games, and they must have a license from the New York State Gaming Commission.

title: Application for Permission to Disburse Net Proceeds of Games of Chance
description: Nonprofit groups need permission to use money from games of chance, and they must have a license from the New York State Gaming Commission.

title: Article 43 Corporation License (Non-Profit Health Service Corporation)
description: In New York State, health maintenance organizations (HMOs) and nonprofit health insurance companies need this license.

title: Assisted Living Residence (ALR) License
description: You need an Assisted Living Residence (ALR) License if your business provides certain care services. The New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) issues this license.

title: Authority to Transport Household Goods
description: This license allows businesses move household items in New York State.

title: Authority to Transport Property (Except Household Goods)
description: Businesses need this permit to transport property that is not considered a household good. Household goods are things like:

title: Bait License
description: A Bait License lets you harvest and sell certain fish and water insects as bait. The New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) gives these licenses.

title: Ball Park / Stadium Beer License
description: Businesses need a Ball Park/Stadium Beer License to sell beer at ballparks, stadiums, racetracks and arenas. The New York State Liquor Authority (SLA) gives this license.

title: Barber Shop Owner or Area Renter License
description: The Barber Shop Owner or Area Renter License lets you own, control or run a barber shop. The New York State Department of State (NYSDOS) gives out these licenses.

title: Bathing Establishment with Pool (Annual & Seasonal)
description: You need a permit to install, run or build any pool in New York City. This rule comes from the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. This includes pools owned by City agencies, businesses or private groups. Examples are:

title: Bathing Establishment without Pool (Steam Room, Sauna and Spray Ground)
description: You need a permit to run a bathing place without a pool in New York City. This includes steam rooms, saunas and spray grounds.

title: Black Car Base License
description: The New York Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) offers a black car base license. This is required if you want to run a business that offers rides in New York City. This is needed for any business that sends cars to pick up people. Your base must have a TLC license to offer rides in New York City. All cars and drivers linked to your base must also have the right licenses from the TLC.

title: Black Car Vehicle License
description: The New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) issues a black car vehicle license. You need this license to use a car for for-hire rides in New York City.

title: Body Damage Estimator License
description: If your business assesses the cost of car body damage, you need a license from the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV).

title: Booting Company License
description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) issues a booting company license. This is needed for any business that will put a device on a parked car to stop it from moving.

title: Cabaret Liquor License
description: If your business has musical entertainment for more than 600 people, you need a Cabaret Liquor License to serve alcohol. The New York State Liquor Authority (NYSLA) issues this license.

title: Captive Insurance Company License
description: Your business can create a company to insure your risks. You need a license from the New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS).

title: Car Wash License
description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection(DCWP) offers a car wash license.

title: Catering Establishment (Liquor) License
description: If your business caters private events at their place of business and serves alcohol, you need a Catering Establishment License from the State Liquor Authority (SLA).

title: Check Casher License
description: Your business needs a license to cash checks in New York State. This license comes from the New York State (NYS) Department of Financial Services (DFS).

title: Coin Processing License
description: If you or your business processes or exchanges coins, you need a license from the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS).

title: Combo Garage and Parking Lot License
description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) offers a license for combo garage and parking lot.

title: Commercial Lessor License
description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) issues a license for commercial lessors. This is needed if your business will rent space to nonprofit groups for charitable games such as bingo and games of chance.

title: Commuter Van Base
description: The New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) gives licenses to businesses to run commuter vans. These vans drive people around New York City. They can carry between 9 and 20 passengers. The vans follow a set schedule. They travel between homes and places such as work, transit stations, shopping centers or recreation areas.

title: Commuter Van Vehicle License
description: A commuter van is a vehicle that can seat 9 to 20 people. The NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) gives licenses to these vans. They can carry passengers for-hire in an Authorized Commuter Van Service.

title: Controlled Substance Activity License
description: If your business makes, sells or uses controlled substances, you need a license from the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH).

title: Cooperative Insurance Company License
description: Cooperative insurance companies need this license to work in New York State. Contact the Department of Financial Services for more details.

title: Dealer in Products for the Disabled License
description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) offers a license for dealing in products for the disabled. This license is needed if you sell, rent, fix or adjust any device for the disabled. This covers braces, crutches and wheelchairs.

title: Debt Collection Agency License
description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) gives the Debt Collection Agency License. If your business collects or tries to collect personal or household debts from New York City residents, you need this license. This rule applies even if your business is outside New York State.

title: Driving School License
description: Driving schools in New York State need a license from the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV). This license lets schools:

title: Drug Store Off-Premise Beer / Wine Products License
description: If your drug store wants to sell beer, cider or wine, you need a special license from the New York State Liquor Authority (SLA).

title: Drug Store Off-Premise Beer License
description: If your drug store wants to sell beer, you need a Drug Store Off-Premise Beer License from the New York State Liquor Authority (SLA).

title: Eating Place Beer License
description: You need an Eating Place Beer License to sell beer and cider at your restaurant. This license does not let you sell wine or liquor. The New York State Liquor Authority (SLA) gives this license.

title: Electronic & Home Appliance Service Dealer License
description: You need an Electronic & Home Appliance Service Dealer license to fix or service electronic items and home appliances. This also includes off-site repairs. The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) gives this license.

title: Electronic Cigarette Retail Dealer License
description: You need a license to sell electronic cigarettes. The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) gives this license.

title: Electronics Store License
description: You need an Electronics Store License if you sell electronic goods. This includes cell phones, tablets, audio equipment, video equipment, photographic equipment, computers or computer equipment, and calculators.

title: Employment Agency License
description: You need an Employment Agency License to help people find jobs for a fee. This includes helping employers find workers. The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) gives this license.

title: Excess Line Broker License (Entity)
description: A business needs this license to buy insurance from companies not licensed in New York State.

title: Exhibiting Exotic Animals
description: You need a permit to exhibit or use any animal in New York City for business. This includes animals in theatrical performances, circuses or wildlife rehabilitator demonstrations.

title: Farm Winery License
description: A Farm Winery License lets you make and sell wine where you grow the fruit. The New York State Liquor Authority (SLA) gives this license.

title: Federal Firearms License
description: Businesses that want to sell or make guns or bullets in the United States need a Federal Firearms License. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) issues out this license.

title: Fill Material Operation
description: You need a Fill Material Operation Permit to do landfilling, grading, land improvements or changing property grades by adding fill material. The New York City Department of Sanitation (DSNY) gives this permit for construction projects in New York City.

title: Financial Guaranty Insurance Corporation
description: This license allows the organization of a domestic stock financial guaranty insurance company in New York State.

title: Firearm Dealer's License
description: You need a Firearms Dealer License to sell handguns or ammunition in New York City.

title: Food Processing Establishment License
description: Any business that sells packaged foods that are ready to eat needs a Food Processing Establishment License from the New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets.

title: Fraternal Benefit Society Admission License
description: This license lets a fraternal benefit society run an insurance business. The business can offer:

title: Frozen Desserts, License to Handle Wholesale
description: You need this license to sell or give out frozen desserts in New York State. The New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets gives this license.

title: Frozen Desserts, License to Manufacture Wholesale
description: You need this license to make frozen desserts in New York State. The New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets gives this license.

title: Games of Chance License
description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) issues a Games of Chance License. You need this license to run games where prizes are given based on chance. This is based on designated numbers, colors or symbols. Only certain groups can get this license. These groups include religious groups, charity groups, veterans' groups and volunteer firefighter groups.

title: Garage License
description: You need a Garage License if your business holds five or more vehicles in a closed space. You must charge a fee, either directly or indirectly. The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) gives out this license.

title: General Insurance Consultant License
description: You need a license to look at insurance policies for money. You also need a license to give advice about insurance.

title: General Vendor Distributor License
description: You need a General Vendor Distributor License if you use motor vehicles to move goods to public places. These places include sidewalks, streets or plazas. This license lets you sell to a general vendor. The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) gives this license.

title: General Vendor License
description: You need a General Vendor License to sell, lease or offer goods or services in a public space that is not a store.

title: Grocery and Drug Store Beer and Wine Product License
description: If you own a grocery or drug store in New York State and want to sell beer, cider or wine, you need a special license. The New York State Liquor Authority (SLA) issues these licenses. You can get the Grocery and Drug Store Beer/Wine Products License or the Grocery Store Beer/Wine Products License.

title: Grocery Store Beer License
description: If you want to sell beer in a grocery store in New York State, you need the Grocery Store Beer License. The New York State Liquor Authority (SLA) gives out this license.

title: Group Family Day Care License
description: Group Family Day Care is child care in a family home on a regular basis. It lasts more than three hours per day per child. This care can include:

title: Home Improvement Contractor License
description: You need a Home Improvement Contractor License to do construction, repair, remodeling or other home improvement work to any residential land or building in New York City. This includes work such as building, replacing or fixing of basements, driveways, fences, garages, landscaping, patios, porches, sidewalks, swimming pools and terraces or any other improvements to structures or land next to a home or apartment building.

title: Home Inspector License
description: Home inspectors need a license from the New York State Department of State (NYSDOS).

title: Horse Drawn Cab Owner License
description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) offers a license for horse-drawn cab owners.

title: Horse Racing License
description: If you want to participate in a horse race in New York State, you need a license. The New York State Gaming Commission gives these licenses.

title: Independent Adjuster License
description: In New York State, you need a license to investigate and adjust insurance claims. For more information, contact the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYS DFS).

title: Industrial Laundry Delivery License
description: You need an Industrial Laundry Delivery License if your business moves certain laundry.

title: Industrial Laundry License
description: A business needs an Industrial Laundry License if it provides laundry services to other businesses like hotels, hospitals, restaurants, gyms and retail laundries, or runs a laundry service in connection with any commercial business, such as a hotel, restaurant or gym.

title: Inspection Station License, Official Business Certificate
description: The New York State DMV issues licenses to inspection stations. These stations check motor vehicles to make sure they are safe and meet emissions rules.

title: License for Waste Removal
description: You need a Trade Waste Removal License for your business to remove, collect or dispose trade waste from businesses in New York City. Trade waste includes regular waste, organic waste, recyclable materials, medical waste and waste materials resulting from building demolition, construction, alteration or excavation. The license lasts for two years.

title: License to Conduct Bingo Games
description: Nonprofit groups need a license to conduct bingo games. They must register with the New York State Gaming Commission. After signing up, they must get a license from the New York City Department of Consumer Affairs.

title: License to Conduct Games of Chance
description: Nonprofit groups need a license to run games of chance. First, they must register with the New York State Gaming Commission. After that, they need a license from the New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP).

title: Licensed Lender
description: This license lets lenders charge interest rates higher than those normally permitted by law.

title: Life Insurance Consultant License
description: In New York State, you need a license to be a life insurance consultant. A consultant provides expert and professional advice on insurance. Licensed consultants cannot sell, solicit or negotiate an insurance policy, as to do so would require licensing as an agent or broker.

title: Life, Accident and Health Insurance Agent License
description: In New York State, you need a special license to sell life and health insurance.

title: Life, Accident and Health Insurance Broker License
description: People and companies need this license to conduct transactions involving life or health insurance.

title: Limited Agent License
description: Businesses that rent certain items need this license to offer insurance for the items rented.

title: Liquor Store License
description: The Liquor Store License lets businesses sell cider, liquor and wine to take home. The New York State Liquor Authority (SLA) gives this license.

title: Livery Car Base License
description: The City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) gives licenses to new livery bases.

title: Livery Car Vehicle License
description: A livery vehicle is a car licensed by the Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC).

title: Lottery Agent License
description: This license lets a store sell New York State Lottery tickets. You must be 18 or older to buy a ticket.

title: Luxury Limo  Base License
description: The City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) gives licenses to businesses that run luxury limos. A Luxury Limo Base uses a radio or other system to send information to drivers of TLC-licensed luxury limos.

title: Luxury Limo  Vehicle License
description: A luxury limousine is a for-hire vehicle.

title: Manufacturing of Frozen Desserts - Retail
description: If you manufacture, process, assemble, freeze or store frozen desserts for distribution or sale to consumers, you need a permit. This permit is from the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH). You need this permit along with any other food permits.

title: Medallion Broker
description: A taxicab broker helps transfer a taxi license (medallion). This can be a person or a business.

title: Medallion Owner, Corporation
description: Medallion owners have a special license. This license lets you own a car that the Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) approves for use as a taxi. Only medallion taxicabs can pick up people who hail them on the street, anywhere in the City. The number of medallions in the City is limited by State law. However, you can transfer a medallion by law and resell it.

title: Milk Dealer License
description: You need a Milk Dealer License to sell, distribute or process unpasteurized milk. The New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets issues this license.

title: Mobile Food Vending License
description: The Mobile Food Vending License lets you make and sell food from a truck or pushcart. The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) gives this license as a photo ID badge. There are no waiting lists to apply for this license.

title: Money Transmitter, License to be a
description: Businesses that sell or issue ways to pay, or send and receive money by wire transfer, need a Money Transmitter License. This license comes from the New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS).

title: Mortgage Guaranty Insurance Company License
description: Companies that sell mortgage guaranty insurance need a license in New York State. There are different licenses for companies in New York and those outside New York.

title: Mortgage Loan Originator License
description: If you provide information for mortgage loans in New York State, you need a Mortgage Loan Originator License. The New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS) gives out these licenses.

title: Mutual Property / Casualty Insurance License
description: Businesses that sell mutual property or casualty insurance in New York State need a license. You need a separate license if your business is based outside New York State.

title: Newsstand License
description: You need a Newsstand License to run a stand on a public sidewalk. This stand is not easy to move. It is mainly for selling newspapers and magazines. You can also sell cigarettes, lottery tickets and snacks if you have the right permits.

title: On Premises Liquor License
description: This license lets you sell liquor, wine, cider and beer at your restaurant, tavern, nightclub, theater or other place. The New York State Liquor Authority (SLA) gives this license.

title: Operate a Bathing Beach
description: All bathing beaches in New York City need a Permit to Operate a Bathing Beach issued by the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH).

title: Operating a Commercial Stable
description: If you keep horses for a fee, you need a permit from the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH). It does not matter if the horses are private or rented (such as for riding lessons or for use with horse-drawn carriages).

title: Paratransit Base License
description: If you want to help people in wheelchairs, you need a Paratransit Base License. Paratransit vehicles are wheelchair-accessible vans. These vans help people who use wheelchairs or need special help in New York City. They have lifts or ramps to help people get in and out.

title: Paratransit Vehicle License
description: To drive a Paratransit vehicle in New York City, you need a Paratransit Vehicle License. This license is for vehicles that help people in wheelchairs get around. The Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) gives out these licenses.

title: Parking Lot License
description: You need a Parking Lot License if your business can hold five or more cars in an open, unenclosed space and charges a fee or other payment either directly or indirectly. The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) gives out this license.

title: Pawnbroker License
description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) gives out the pawnbroker license. A pawnbroker, also called a "collateral loan broker," is a person, partnership or company that loans money on personal items or buys personal items and sells them back at a set price. This is defined in New York State General Business Law (GBL) §52.

title: Pedicab Business License
description: The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) offers a license for pedicab businesses.

title: Performing Work on a Landmarked Property
description: If you own a landmark or a building in a designated historic district in New York City, you need a permit from the Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) before doing any work. You also need a permit from LPC for any work that needs a permit from the Department of Buildings (DOB).

title: Pet Cemetery and Pet Crematorium, License to Operate a
description: This license lets you run a pet cemetery or pet crematorium in New York State. The New York State Department of State (NYSDOS) gives out this license.

title: Pet Dealer License
description: If you sell more than nine dogs or cats each year, you need a Pet Dealer License. The New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets gives out this license.

title: Petting Zoos
description: If you want to run a petting zoo in New York City, you need a permit from the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) Office of Veterinary Public Health Services (VPHS).

title: Private Community Sewage Disposal System
description: You need this permit to build and run private sewage systems in subdivision realty developments with 15 or more homes.

title: Private Investigator Branch Office License
description: Branch offices for private investigators need their own licenses. The New York State Department of State (NYSDOS) gives these licenses.

title: Process Serving Agency License
description: You need a Process Serving Agency License if you or your business assigns, distributes or delivers process to another for actual service. The New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) gives this license.

title: Property / Casualty Insurance Agents and Brokers
description: To sell or manage property insurance in New York State, you need a license. There are two types of licenses:

title: Public Adjuster License
description: If you want to negotiate settlements for people with fire damage claims, you need a public adjuster license.

title: Radioactive Materials License
description: Businesses that use radioactive materials need a license. This license comes from the New York State Department of Health (DOH). These materials can be used for business or science.

title: Radiological Materials Licensing
description: The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) controls the possession and use of radioactive material in New York City. The DOHMH does this for the United States Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The DOHMH Office of Radiological Health checks and licenses materials for medical, academic and research use in the City.

title: Raw Milk Dealer License
description: Dairy farmers need a Raw Milk Dealer License to sell raw milk. The New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets gives this license.

title: Real Estate Branch Office, License to Operate a
description: This permit lets a real estate broker run a branch office. Each branch office needs its own permit.

title: Reciprocal Insurance License
description: Businesses in a reciprocal insurance arrangement need a license. There are different licenses for businesses inside and outside New York State.

title: Reinsurance Intermediary License
description: If you sell or negotiate reinsurance contracts, you need a license. This rule is for both businesses and individuals. Each must have a separate license.

title: Restaurant Wine License
description: The State Liquor Authority (SLA) gives this license to restaurants. It lets them sell wine and beer. They cannot sell liquor. Customers can drink these on the premises.

title: Retail Food Store License
description: If you sell food for people to take home, you need a Retail Food Store License. This includes selling foods like milk, eggs and meat. The New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets gives out this license.

title: Rifle / Shotgun Dealer License
description: A Rifle / Shotgun Dealer's License is needed for any business that sells rifles, shotguns or ammunition in New York City.

title: Sale of Small Animals (Pet Shops)
description: Pet shops that sell animals need a permit from the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH). Starting December 15, 2024, pet shops cannot sell dogs or cats.

title: Scale Dealer or Repairer License
